articles.title: Furious Locals Block Famous Beach as Overtourism Protests Intensify at Vacation Hot Spot
articles.summary: The sand at Cala Saladeta, one of Ibiza’s most photographed coves, was covered with beach towels and angry banners rather than sunbathers last week. Around a...
articles.body:
Residents in Ibiza staged a protest at Cala Saladeta beach against overtourism, accusing the tourism industry of overwhelming public spaces and driving up the cost of living.

Activists in Spain are demanding a different tourism model that puts greater emphasis on residents and limits the growth of visitor numbers, framing tourism as an existential threat to local identity rather than just an inconvenience.

Anti-tourism demonstrations have intensified across Spain, with protesters in Barcelona spraying visitors with water guns and chanting "tourists go home," part of a larger movement against mass tourism in southern Europe's top destinations.

The sand at Cala Saladeta, one of Ibiza's most photographed coves, was covered with beach towels and angry banners rather than sunbathers last week. Around a hundred residents staged a coordinated occupation of the beach, turning a strip of turquoise water into the latest flashpoint in Spain's spiraling battle over mass tourism. It's a scene that has now played out, in one form or another, across half a dozen European destinations over the past two summers, and it shows no sign of losing momentum.

What began as scattered grumbling about crowded promenades has hardened into an organized, increasingly confrontational movement. Locals from the Balearic Islands to the Canaries to the Portuguese coast are no longer just complaining. They're occupying beaches, spraying tourists with water guns, and marching by the thousands to demand that their governments finally put limits on an industry many now blame for pricing them out of their own hometowns.

The Ibiza Beach Takeover That Sparked New Headlines

About 100 residents gathered at Cala Saladeta beach last week in a dramatic protest against overtourism, with demonstrators accusing the island's booming tourism industry of overwhelming public spaces and driving up the cost of living. [1] The demonstration was organized by the Ibiza Youth Association, a group of young islanders who say residents are increasingly struggling to enjoy their own beaches during the summer. [1] Protesters didn't hold back on messaging either, with one sign summing up the frustration of an entire generation of islanders.

Protesters carried signs criticizing the crush of visitors, including one that read, "Wherever you look, it's all tourists." Organizers also declared that public spaces should remain accessible to locals and that "the island was not for sale." [1] The numbers help explain the anger. Known to locals as Eivissa, Ibiza received nearly 1.2 million tourists in the second quarter of 2025, according to data from the Balearic Islands Statistics Institute. [2] For an island with a permanent population of roughly 160,000 people, that kind of seasonal influx transforms daily life almost overnight.

Beyond Crowded Sand: Housing and Culture Under Pressure

The Ibiza protest wasn't really about beach towels and elbow room, even if that's the image that traveled furthest. Activists have blamed mass tourism for soaring housing costs, pressure on infrastructure and the erosion of local culture. [1] They are demanding a different tourism model that puts greater emphasis on residents and limits the growth of visitor numbers. [1] That framing, tourism as an existential threat to local identity rather than just an inconvenience, has become the dominant narrative across Spain's protest movement.

It's also spreading well beyond one island. The backlash isn't limited to Ibiza. Anti-tourism demonstrations have intensified across Spain, including on neighboring Mallorca and in Barcelona, as residents complain about overcrowding, housing costs and the impact of millions of visitors. [1] Organizers in Ibiza have also signaled that the beach occupation was just an opening move in a longer campaign, not a one-off stunt.

No single image captured this movement's mood quite like Barcelona's water gun protests. Protesters in Barcelona have sprayed visitors with water as part of a demonstration against mass tourism. Demonstrators marching through areas popular with tourists chanted "tourists go home" and squirted them with water pistols, while others carried signs with slogans including "Barcelona is not for sale." [3] According to Barcelona's City Council, some 2,800 people demonstrated against mass tourism in the center of Barcelona. [3]

The tactic returned the following summer, and this time it was described as part of something bigger. The marches were part of the first coordinated effort by activists concerned with the ills of overtourism across southern Europe's top destinations. [4] Protesters in Barcelona blew whistles and held up homemade signs saying "One more tourist, one less resident." They stuck stickers saying "Citizen Self-Defense," in Catalan, and "Tourist Go Home," in English, with a drawing of a water pistol on the doors of hotels and hostels. [4] City officials have responded with genuinely dramatic policy, announcing plans to phase out short-term rental licenses entirely by 2028, though critics argue the move alone won't fix the underlying housing crunch.

The Canary Islands Say "We Have a Limit"

Few slogans have traveled as far as "Canarias tiene un límite," the rallying cry that has turned into an entire protest movement across Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, and the archipelago's other islands. Around 30,000 people took to the streets of the different cities and towns of the archipelago under the banner "The Canary Islands have a limit." [5] The scale of tourism driving that anger is hard to overstate.

In 2023 over 16 million tourists visited and it's likely that number will be higher when 2024 is over. Tourists spent more than 20 billion euros in 2023, but it comes at a price. [5] That price, according to residents, includes being squeezed out of the housing market entirely. Locals are also facing rising costs due to mass tourism. The inflow of tourists has inflated property prices, making it difficult for younger residents to find affordable housing. As rental rates continue to rise, many locals are being pushed out of their communities. [6] Even record visitor numbers haven't slowed the demonstrations; if anything, they've fueled them further.

articles.title: California’s Paradise High lost its town to fire in 2018 and Lahainaluna endured the Lahaina fire in 2023; their football teams have now met in Hawaii for the first ‘Unity Bowl’
articles.summary: US News: Two football teams separated by thousands of miles recently met on a Hawaiian field with a story that went far beyond the scoreboard. Both schools hai.
articles.body: Two football teams separated by thousands of miles recently met on a Hawaiian field with a story that went far beyond the scoreboard. Both schools hail from communities ravaged by devastating wildfires and their initial meeting was intended to be a celebration of survival, rebuilding and the connections made from shared loss. Three years after the Maui wildfire and nearly eight years after the Camp Fire that destroyed Paradise, Paradise High School in California headed to Maui for the inaugural Unity Bowl against Lahainaluna High School. Most of the players at Paradise High were in elementary school when the 2018 Camp Fire tore through Butte County. As reported by Maui Now, on Nov. 8, 2018, the Camp Fire in Paradise displaced more than 50,000 people, destroyed over 18,000 structures and killed 85 people, marking it as the deadliest wildfire in US history at the time. Five years later, on Aug. 8, 2023, a wildfire tore through Lahaina and destroyed more than 2,200 buildings, killing 102 people in the deadliest wildfire in U.S. history. The fire also decimated Paradise, and residents tried to pick up their lives after widespread destruction. Lahainaluna High students on Maui faced a similar disruption after the August 2023 wildfire destroyed Lahaina. Many of the current seniors at the school were freshmen when the fire happened and still live with its effects. In both communities, their high school football programs have been important sources of identity and pride in difficult times. The Unity Bowl unites those experiences in sport, giving players from both schools a chance to meet others who understand what it means to rebuild after catastrophe.A meeting years in the makingThe concept for the showdown began in 2024 when Paradise High administrators reached out to Lahainaluna about establishing a home-and-home series. The first game was played at Sue D. Cooley Stadium, with Lahainaluna as the host on September 5. The schools also are planning a return meet in Paradise in 2027. Paradise made it to Maui after fundraising efforts helped cover the cost of the long trip from Northern California. Contributors included NFL quarterback and Butte County native Aaron Rodgers, who donated $15,000 toward the trip.More than a football weekenderThe teams’ visit was way beyond game day. Players, coaches and parents from both programs came together for a community event at the OUTRIGGER Kāʻanapali Beach Resort. The players also had a chance to experience local culture and spend time together off the field with a lūʻau put on with Maui chef Zach Sato. The gatherings were designed to join young people who have suffered eerily similar disruptions while growing up on different sides of the Pacific.Football: a source of strengthBoth programs have shown in the past how sport can bring communities back to a sense of normalcy. Paradise’s 2019 season started with 12 straight wins, its first season after the Camp Fire. Lahainaluna has been one of Maui’s dominant football programs for more than a decade and has won multiple state titles. The Lunas' impressive 46-game streak of Maui Interscholastic League wins ended in 2024 but the team bounced back to make the state playoff and Paradise entered the Unity Bowl this season at 1-1, Lahainaluna at 0-2. But the records matter less than the meaning attached to the meeting.A new tradition born from tragedyFor the Lahainaluna seniors, the game holds special personal significance. Some still live away from their homes, which have not yet been rebuilt after the Lahaina fire. Paradise’s players have also been displaced and rebuilt a community, but at a much younger age. Their common experiences create a rare opportunity for intergenerational and inter-geographic connections. The Unity Bowl is not just a first-time football matchup. Two communities finding common ground, letting their youngest generation turn painful memories into lasting friendships.Image Courtesy: Hawaiʻi DOECatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Truth behind claim that Trump's H-1B fee plan could push cost above $200,000: Here's the calculation
articles.summary: US News: The cost of hiring a foreign skilled worker through the H-1B visa programme could cross $200,000 under a new Trump administration proposal, USA Today .
articles.body: The cost of hiring a foreign skilled worker through the H-1B visa programme could cross $200,000 under a new Trump administration proposal, USA Today reported, combining the earlier proposal of $100K fee and the new proposal of $103,265 fee. The earlier fee got blocked by a court while the new fee is a proposal by the Department of Homeland Security.If there was already a $100,000 H-1B fee, is the new $103,265 charge replacing it, or could employers have to pay both?The answer is both.Why are there two H-1B fees?The two charges come from different mechanisms.The earlier $100,000 payment was imposed through a presidential proclamation signed by President Donald Trump in September 2025. It applied to certain H-1B workers entering the US from abroad. But a federal judge struck down that payment requirement in June 2026, ruling it unlawful. The Trump administration has appealed the decision. The $100,000 payment is therefore not currently being collected.The new $103,265 charge is different. DHS is attempting to establish it through formal rulemaking. The proposal was published in the Federal Register on August 24 and would apply to cap-subject H-1B petitions, including petitions qualifying for the advanced-degree exemption. It would not apply to cap-exempt H-1B petitions.So could an employer actually pay $203,265?Yes, theoretically. If Trump's initial fee is upheld and the new fee also become a rule and not get legally blocked.The department considered simply increasing an existing H-1B fee but instead proposed creating the $103,265 charge as a separate fee. The Federal Register notice specifically said it would be in addition to other applicable fees or payments, including a separate payment required under a presidential proclamation.DHS said that if a petitioner is subject to both the proclamation payment and the new H-1B fee, the petitioner would have to pay both amounts.That means a case theoretically subject to both could face:$100,000 — the earlier presidential-proclamation payment$103,265 — the newly proposed DHS fee$203,265 combinedPlus the ordinary H-1B filing and other applicable feesNeither of the two six-figure charges is currently functioning as a $203,265 combined fee.Why is DHS proposing the $103,265 fee?DHS says the new fee is intended to recover costs associated with administering the lawful immigration system across federal agencies. The department estimates that the fee could generate billions of dollars annually. It expects the charge to apply to approximately 85,000 cap-subject H-1B petitions each year under its projections.The proposal would also be imposed separately from existing H-1B fees.The USA Today report said only 85 applicants paid the $100K fee during the first five months before they were blocked in court. But because the number of applicants dropped 87%, the agency collected $28 million less during that period.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Federal regulators said the two crew members aboard the Amazon cargo jet that crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday survived the accident. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) provided the update during a Sunday press conference after officials said the cargo plane overran the runway and caught fire while landing. The crash killed five people and injured five others, authorities said Sunday. The jet collided with two vehicles carrying at least eight occupants, according to NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy. Seven of the victims were in a van that was struck and "torn apart" on airport grounds, Homendy said. The 2012 white Ford Econoline van was owned by Ocean Service Corporation, a contract cleaning company that provides services for airlines, she said. AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED The NTSB said the aircraft then crashed through the airport perimeter and struck a civilian vehicle, a Toyota Corolla Cross LE, that was traveling on Northwest 67th Avenue. Homendy said investigators observed what appeared to be deployed airbags in the vehicles as they surveyed the crash site. "You can see components from vehicles, both passenger vehicles and the aircraft itself," Homendy said. The jet then "continued into the grass and impacted another fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed," Homendy said. In total, the jet reportedly traveled 1,300 feet beyond the paved surface. Homendy said the wreckage was "extensive," noting that the crash damaged airport navigational aids and equipment, while fencing was ripped apart throughout the area. The aircraft traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, then from Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico, before returning to Miami, Homendy said. NTSB investigators have recovered the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder, which they planned to examine. The kitchen island is lined with metallic silver barstools and matching placemats, giving the space a polished, contemporary look.The kitchen opens directly into the living room, where Kai has kept the decor relatively understated. A large white sofa with wide seats dominates the room, complemented by grey throw pillows.The apartment also features a fireplace, which Kai singled out as one of the coolest elements of her home.“Got my fireplace, which is like I think the coolest part of this,” she said while walking viewers through the space.Kai adds personal touches to her Miami homeDespite the apartment’s polished interiors, Kai has added several personal touches that reflect her interests and family.She pointed out an Aspen-themed piece that she said she had hung herself, explaining that she loves skiing and Aspen. articles.title: Kick streamer Binx sparks fury after taking ‘disrespectful’ photo beside Amazon plane crash that killed five in Miami
articles.summary: US Streamers News: A Kick streamer known as Binx is facing backlash after appearing to take a photo beside the wreckage of an Amazon cargo plane that crashed at Miami In.
articles.body: A Kick streamer known as Binx is facing backlash after appearing to take a photo beside the wreckage of an Amazon cargo plane that crashed at Miami International Airport, killing five people. The incident happened on September 6, when the Boeing 767-300, operated by 21 Air for Amazon Prime Air, overran the runway and hit several vehicles. Five others were injured, including three who were critically hurt. The cause of the crash is still being investigated, and it is not yet clear whether those killed were inside the plane or on the ground. The BBC reported the latest details on the crash.Kick streamer Binx approaches Amazon plane wreckage after fatal crashHours after the crash, Binx went near the damaged aircraft while livestreaming in Miami. Footage shared online appears to show her getting close to the plane’s burnt nose and wings before posing for a photograph.At one point, Binx told a person with her to “take a picture of us”. As they moved closer to the wreckage, she was also heard repeatedly saying, “hurry, take a picture.”The scene quickly drew criticism because the crash had killed five people only hours earlier. One person reacted: “WTF. People died here. Have some respect,” while another wrote, “Film yourselves committing a felony… Darwin award.”Other comments were also harsh. One person called the act “pretty disrespectful and heartless,” while another said, “This will get her in trouble with federal authorities.”According to Need To Know, footage showed Binx crossing a barrier before reaching the wreckage. The report also said a man later confronted the group and told them they were on private property. Binx reportedly apologised and left.Daniella Levine Cava confirms five deaths as investigation continuesThe crash involved Prime Air Flight 7598, which had arrived from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The plane went beyond the runway at around 2 p.m., crossed a road and struck multiple vehicles before catching fire. More than 60 Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units responded, with around 200 emergency personnel involved in the rescue effort.Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said five people were killed and five others were injured. Three of those injured were in critical condition. She also said emergency crews reached the scene within “seconds” of the crash.The National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration are investigating what caused the plane to overrun the runway. Officials have not yet said whether weather, the landing or another factor played a role.The issue of Binx’s access to the area could also raise questions. Federal law, under 49 U.S.C. §46314, bars knowingly entering certain aircraft or airport areas in violation of security rules. The basic offence can carry up to one year in prison, while a maximum of 10 years applies in specific cases involving an intent to evade security procedures or commit a felony. It has not been established that the law applies to Binx or that she will face charges.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Company can be punished for offence carrying imprisonment, term can be replaced by fine: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: A company having no physical body cannot be imprisoned and having no mind cannot possess mens rea (guilty mind), which is essential for con.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A company having no physical body cannot be imprisoned and having no mind cannot possess mens rea (guilty mind), which is essential for conviction in a criminal case. So can a firm be convicted and punished?SC Monday answered the tricky questions by holding that a company can be convicted even when it cannot have a guilty mind of its own and can also be punished, though the punishment of a jail term can be substituted by a fine.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Manoj Misra said there is a need to bring a law for corporate criminal liability but said the issue comes within the legislature's prerogative and it cannot be done by a court. It held that a company is not rendered immune to prosecution merely because the offence carries a mandatory sentence of imprisonment. Referring to a constitution bench ruling, the bench said a judicial discretion to impose a fine alone must be read into such provisions when dealing with juristic persons."The position under Indian law is thus clear that a corporation can be prosecuted for an offence notwithstanding that it carries a mandatory sentence of imprisonment or requires proof of mens rea. It appears that a corporation cannot be prosecuted only where the offence is punishable with imprisonment alone, or where the offence, by its nature, requires personal malicious intent, such that it is incapable of commission by a corporation at all," the bench said. SC passed the order on a plea by Sanofi India Ltd which said a prosecution against a corporation like it, for an offence requiring mens rea, is maintainable only where a natural person has been identified and arraigned as an accused alongside it. It said that corporations alone cannot be convicted and pleaded that proceedings against it should be quashed. Rejecting the plea of the company, the bench said non-identification of the natural person does not, by itself, render the allegations incapable of disclosing the corporation's role in the offence.The case pertains to the supply of pharmaceutical products by Sanofi India to Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. As per CBI, a BARC officer had conspired with the company to procure medicines at inflated prices and in quantities exceeding the requirement. A case was registered against Sanofi, which challenged its prosecution on the ground that none of its employees had been made accused and a company alone cannot be prosecuted."... where the surrounding facts and circumstances, taken as a whole, disclose the possibility that the corporation acted with the requisite mens rea, that disclosure is not defeated merely because no particular individual has been identified as its source. Therefore, the ingredient of mens rea can still be disclosed even where no individual has been identified," the bench said while rejecting the plea of the company.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Metallica's Lars Ulrich once planned a $40 million mansion on this California ridge; now 161 acres are being preserved as public open space
articles.summary: Rest of World News: For years, a ridgeline in Marin County carried the possibility of becoming the private retreat of Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich. The 161-acre property.
articles.body: For years, a ridgeline in Marin County carried the possibility of becoming the private retreat of Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich. The 161-acre property on King Mountain was once slated for a sprawling residence, and Ulrich later pursued plans for an architect-designed compound of his own, complete with space for music archives, a recording studio and a workroom. Construction even reached the foundation before the project was abandoned. The mountaintop then remained privately held, despite sitting alongside public open space and offering wide views across Mount Tamalpais, Tiburon and San Pablo Bay.Now its future is changing in a very different direction. The land has been acquired through a conservation deal and is being transferred to Marin County, protecting it from residential development. Once the necessary work is completed, part of the previously inaccessible summit is expected to open to the public, turning a site once intended for a private mansion into protected open space.Ulrich's ambitious plans for the King Mountain ridgeUlrich's connection to the property dates back to the early 2000s, when the Metallica drummer began developing plans for a substantial compound on the King Mountain ridge.The proposed house was designed by architect Stanley Saitowitz. It was far removed from a conventional suburban mansion. Plans showed a modern, low-profile structure built around the hillside, with large areas of glass and separate spaces intended for Ulrich's work and music collection.The design included a music archive, recording studio and work room. Construction actually got as far as the foundation before the project was abandoned.The property was subsequently placed on the market. At one stage, the asking price was around $40 million, although later listings were considerably lower. Despite the property's development potential, no private estate ultimately appeared on the ridge.King Mountain's summit stayed private for decadesThe 161-acre property had been the subject of planning battles and conservation efforts for decades. In the 1990s, a previous owner secured approval for a residential compound of roughly 27,500 square feet. The plans demonstrated just how different the summit might have looked if the development had gone ahead.The approvals remained in place even as ownership changed.Meanwhile, Marin County had been building its own patchwork of protected land around the mountain. Existing portions of the King Mountain Open Space Preserve were acquired in 1989 and 1990, while the county also held scenic and trail easements across parts of the privately owned property. The result was a public trail system that effectively surrounded land people could not enter. The summit itself remained the missing piece.A conservation deal finally secured King Mountain's summitThe breakthrough came in 2026, when the Marin Open Space Trust negotiated to buy the 161-acre property with funding from the Shelby Cullom Davis Charitable Fund.The trust then arranged for the land to be donated to the Marin County Open Space District. On July 14, the district board approved the agreements, clearing the way for the property to become part of the King Mountain Open Space Preserve.The transaction will expand the preserve from 108 acres to approximately 269 acres. More importantly for visitors, about 32 acres around the summit that had been off limits will eventually become accessible to the public.The $2 million plan to prepare King Mountain for public useThe new arrangement removes the possibility of the summit becoming another large private residential estate.That matters because the high ground is not simply a viewpoint. The summit contains native prairie and hardwood forest, along with broad views across the surrounding landscape. From the top, visitors can see Mount Tamalpais, the Tiburon Peninsula and San Pablo Bay.The conservation purchase also comes with money for looking after the property. The Davis charitable fund is providing a $2 million stewardship fund to support management and public-access work for at least a decade.Some of the initial work is fairly practical. Plans include removing sections of fencing, taking down a guardhouse, tackling invasive vegetation and installing signs. Picnic tables are also planned near the summit.The mountain therefore will not simply change ownership and immediately look different. Some of the physical traces of its private past have to be removed first.From private compound to public open spaceThere is a strange symmetry to the property's history. The mountaintop was once seen as the site for a large estate. Ulrich's plans took that idea further, with a purpose-built home designed around music, work and the views from the ridge. A foundation was poured, but the house was never completed.Years later, the same 161 acres are being secured for a purpose that requires no mansion at all.The county's existing preserve will stretch across the mountain, connecting previously separated pieces of public land. The summit, once the part people could see but not reach, will become the part they can finally walk to.For King Mountain, the most significant change is not the end of an old building proposal. It is what replaces it: a protected ridgeline, native habitat and a public viewpoint where a private compound might once have stood.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Netas need to be told assault on docs won't be tolerated: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Taking note of another instance of a Shiv Sena politician in Maharashtra assaulting doctors, Supreme Court Monday said the situation in the.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Taking note of another instance of a Shiv Sena politician in Maharashtra assaulting doctors, Supreme Court Monday said the situation in the state had worsened and favoured strict action against politicians to send a message that such behaviour against a medical practitioner would not be tolerated.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said people indulging in violence against doctors should be arrested without any delay. "They do not deserve to roam around," the bench said while referring to the recent incident of Sena workers assaulting doctors and hospital staff in Palghar.SC made the observations while hearing the plea of Sena corporator Ramesh Sukrya Mhatre, who is accused of assaulting doctors at Dombivli in July. He had moved SC against stringent conditions imposed by HC on him while granting bail last month. Sensing the mood of the court, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi sought to withdraw the petition.The court allowed his plea for the withdrawal but before that, it expressed its concern over the growing number of incidents of doctors being attacked by politicians and said that it cannot be justified.Rohatgi said the group of people responsible for the assault in Palghar was different, but SC said they belonged to the same party. "Same ideology. How can this be justified that you go and assault them inside their chambers and beat them brutally? It's an issue of law and public order," the bench said. Mhatre was arrested in July for allegedly assaulting doctors and staff at a civic-run hospital in Dombivli on July 6.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Resolution doesn't endorse any specific map: MEA
articles.summary: India News: India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution, \"Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic R.
articles.body: India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution, "Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World's Regions, Particularly Africa".MEA said the resolution's purpose is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses, and it neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names."India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation, stressing the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation. We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries," said Randhir Jaiswal.The resolution received abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against it from US.The resolution noted that the Mercator projection remains widely used in educational, media, digital and official materials, despite the considerable distortion of landmasses to the North and South, far from the equator.It expressed concern that this distortion contributed to minimising the perceived sizes of Africa, Latin America and South Asia, and perpetuating an unbalanced view of the world. India welcomed the intention behind the resolution to promote more accurate and representative cartographic practices.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Haredi protest against light rail construction erupts on Jerusalem's Bar-Ilan Street
articles.summary: Police said activists tried to block traffic and damage the construction sites, and officers began dispersing the crowd after declaring the demonstration ill...
articles.body:
Ultra-Orthodox Jewish protesters in Jerusalem set fire to construction materials and blocked traffic during a demonstration against the expansion of the light rail network on Bar-Ilan Street.

Police declared the protest illegal and began dispersing the crowd after activists attempted to damage construction sites along the light rail route.

Haredi protests against the light rail project have resulted in over NIS 400 million in damages to the unfinished Green Line, causing delays and changes to the route.

Police said activists tried to block traffic and damage the construction sites, and officers began dispersing the crowd after declaring the demonstration illegal.

Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) protesters demonstrated against light rail construction on Bar-Ilan Street in Jerusalem on Monday, according to the Israel Police.

Police said activists tried to block traffic and damage the construction sites, and officers began dispersing the crowd after declaring the protest unlawful.

The demonstration marks the latest in what have become regular protests against the expansion of Jerusalem's light rail network along Bar-Ilan Street.

On August 27, hundreds of haredi individuals gathered in the same area to protest the project, with Ynet News reporting that several demonstrators tore down fences, set fire to cardboard installations , and attempted to break into the construction site.

A suspect in the alleged arson was later arrested by police and taken in for questioning. An additional suspect was arrested for throwing stones at security forces.

Haredi protests cause over NIS 400 million in damage to light rail

The protests follow an N12 News report that haredi protests have cumulatively caused over NIS 400 million in damage to the Jerusalem Light Rail's unfinished Green Line since construction began about six years ago.

The protests have caused Jerusalem Light Rail operator Cfir to change opening dates and routing in several sections of the line, according to N12.

Walla and Alon Hachmon contributed to this report.
